assets.overview: Aerodrome Finance began as a Base DEX, but the official upgrade hub says Aerodrome and Velodrome became the unified Aero protocol on October 21, 2026. assets.overview: Ethereum remains a proof-of-stake smart-contract and settlement platform whose roadmap spans Layer 1 capacity, rollup data availability, account usability and privacy. The official roadmap lists Fusaka as in production and Glamsterdam as in development for Q4 2026, not as a completed November upgrade. The Ethereum Foundation's November 6 post highlighted Nym's browser mixnet SDK as a way for wallets and applications to reduce access-layer metadata leakage. Separately, EIP-8297 and EIP-8347 describe a proposed Partitioned Binary Tree and offline migration, but both remain drafts and the migration proposal does not schedule activation. Next checks are coordinated client releases, test results, an explicit Glamsterdam activation announcement and identifiable wallet integrations rather than treating research goals as delivered functionality. Execution complexity, staking/operator concentration and application or bridge failures remain risks that must be distinguished from failure of Ethereum consensus itself.

marketAlerts.change: Keplr social-login breach: Web3Auth says many 'drained' wallets were whitehat rescues
marketAlerts.summary: Keplr confirmed unauthorized transactions from some Google/Apple-login wallets after Web3Auth reported a security issue in its infrastructure that exposed private keys, and both paused social login. On Nov 8 (06:23-06:31 UTC), Web3Auth and Keplr published verified recovery addresses on Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Celestia, Akash, Noble, Injective, dYdX, Babylon, Axelar, Saga, Agoric and one EVM address. They said funds sent there were moved by a whitehat rescue of exposed wallets, not by the attacker. These include the two addresses Bitquery had counted as attacker collectors (~$6.0M across ~44,000 wallets), so that figure now largely describes rescued funds, not confirmed theft. No official loss total has been published, and the rescue is still ongoing. Recovery-phrase and hardware wallets are reported unaffected. On Nov 9 Web3Auth published further verified recovery addresses across dozens of Cosmos and other networks and warned users about impersonators and fake recovery requests.
marketAlerts.why: A shared login and key-management provider exposed keys across many Cosmos chains at once. The confirmed theft amount is now unclear and has not been shown to exceed ~$10M, so this stays Medium. Per Keplr, social-login users should send no new funds to those accounts, should move remaining liquid assets to a recovery-phrase or hardware wallet, and should ignore 'recovery' DMs.

marketAlerts.change: LNbits tells every operator to shut down servers after fund-draining attacks
marketAlerts.summary: LNbits, the open-source Lightning wallet and accounts layer, told all operators on Nov 8 (7:56 AM CST) to stop their servers immediately after a wave of attacks, about 80 minutes after first warning Paywall-extension users. It disabled every instance on its hosted my.lnbits.com service and said services would resume within 24 hours, with patches expected in 24 to 48 hours. One operator (BitTipBot) reported 2,285,545 sats (about 0.023 BTC) withdrawn by newly created accounts before shutdown. LNbits has not disclosed the vulnerability, affected versions or a total loss figure.
marketAlerts.why: This is an application-layer incident, not a flaw in Bitcoin or the Lightning protocol, but LNbits sits behind many tipping bots, point-of-sale setups and custodial Lightning wallets, so a shutdown order affects a broad slice of small Lightning services. Confirmed losses so far are small; it stays Medium until patches ship and a total is known.

marketAlerts.change: Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge exploited for about $0.3M
marketAlerts.summary: Blockaid flagged an ongoing exploit of Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge at 2:42 AM CST on Nov 9: five withdrawals, referencing one small Optimism deposit, drained about $292,000 of locked assets (ankrETH, ankrPOL, ANKR and others) to a new wallet. SlowMist later put losses near $304,500 and said all five forged receipts carried valid signatures from the bridge's trusted signers; whether signer keys were compromised is still under investigation. Blockaid also reported the attacker swept several Ankr operator wallets on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Linea hours earlier. Ankr had not published a post-mortem at review time.
marketAlerts.why: The dollar loss is below the High threshold, but valid-signature forged receipts point at signer or key compromise rather than a simple contract bug, which is the failure mode that matters for every multisig-verified bridge. Exchanges paused related deposits as a precaution.

marketAlerts.change: Initia halts its L1 after unauthorized transfers from rollup escrow accounts
marketAlerts.summary: Initia said it halted its Layer 1 at 06:18 UTC on Nov 10 (12:18 AM CST), in coordination with validators, after finding unauthorized transfers from the escrow accounts that hold assets bridged to several rollups. Earlier on Nov 9 it had paused rollups while investigating an issue in rollup infrastructure. Reported preliminary losses are about $605,000 in USDC moved out via Noble plus roughly $10,000 in other tokens, attributed to compromised rollup infrastructure keys. The investigation is ongoing and the chain remains halted.
marketAlerts.why: A full chain halt after a key-compromise drain is a reminder that bridged-asset escrows and rollup operator keys are concentrated points of failure. The loss is small, but it is Initia's second disruption in weeks and none of the focus networks is directly involved.

news.title: Formation tells the SEC it will run the first tokenized-securities venue on Solana
news.body: Formation Securities notified the SEC on Nov 9 that it intends to operate a tokenized securities venue on Solana under the SEC's Innovation Exemption, and posted the required public notice the same day. Trading runs through permissioned automated-market-maker pools built on licensed Orca contracts, with no order book, and only wallets that pass identity, sanctions and wallet screening can trade or add liquidity. Tokenized shares must carry the same voting and dividend rights as the listed originals, and they can be paired only with non-security crypto assets or tokenized money-market funds. Trading is expected to start in early 2027 with tokenized Exodus, Forward Industries and Galaxy Digital shares, with Superstate and Securitize expected to supply them and Anchorage, BitGo, Fireblocks, Jito's JTX, Solflare and Squads named as access routes. The notice is not an SEC approval, and the exemption caps listed securities and trading volume.
news.why: This is the first named venue to use the new SEC exemption on Solana, putting US-listed equities on a public, permissionless chain with atomic settlement. It turns Solana's tokenization story into a specific regulated product with a launch window, though nothing trades until early 2027 and the venue keeps admin, pause and allowlist control over its contracts.
news.tagReason: A concrete regulated tokenized-equities venue chose Solana, with a dated launch window and named partners.
news.summary: Formation Securities filed notice to run a permissioned tokenized-stock venue on Solana, targeting early 2027.

news.title: Schwab Crypto adds SOL, with AVAX and LINK, for eligible US retail clients
news.body: Charles Schwab said on Nov 9 that Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink are now available to buy and sell through Schwab Crypto, alongside bitcoin and ether, making five assets in total. Schwab Crypto opened to early-access clients in May and to all eligible retail clients in October; it charges 75 basis points per trade and is offered in every US state except New York and Louisiana. The crypto sits in a separate Schwab Premier Bank account linked to the brokerage account, and Schwab acts as custodian, so clients do not hold their own keys. Schwab first announced these three additions in August and says more assets will follow over time.
news.why: Schwab, with about 40 million brokerage accounts, picking SOL as one of its first three altcoins puts Solana in front of mainstream investors inside the same app they use for stocks. It is custodial brokerage access rather than onchain usage, so it widens distribution without directly adding network activity.
news.tagReason: A top US brokerage now offers SOL directly to retail clients, a major distribution step.
news.summary: Schwab Crypto now lists SOL (plus AVAX and LINK) for eligible US retail clients.

news.title: NEAR Intents goes live inside Talos's institutional trading system
news.body: NEAR said on Nov 9 that NEAR Intents is now live in Talos's Order and Execution Management System, so Talos's institutional clients can source cross-chain liquidity through the same request-for-quote workflow they already use. Orders are filled by competing solvers that can draw on more than 30 chains and centralized venues, and clients keep their existing custody integrations. Fungible tokens are supported now; tokenized real-world assets, yield-bearing assets and prediction markets are listed as next. NEAR cites more than $37 billion in total Intents volume and over $4 billion in the past 30 days, and Talos's head of provider network is quoted in the announcement.
news.why: Talos is plumbing used by large trading desks, so this puts NEAR's intents layer directly into institutional order flow rather than asking desks to adopt new tools. Integration is not yet proof of volume from Talos clients; that will show up only in later Intents data.
news.tagReason: A live institutional distribution integration for NEAR's main product, confirmed by both sides.
news.summary: NEAR Intents is live in Talos's OEMS, giving institutional desks solver-sourced cross-chain liquidity.

news.title: Elysium mainnet goes live with Bankr on day one, and Upbit lists HYPE
news.body: Kinetiq and Elysium both posted that Elysium mainnet was live on Nov 9 at about 7 AM CST, and Bankr said Elysium is now live in its agent, letting users launch, trade and track Elysium tokens by chat. Elysium is Kinetiq's HYPE-gas Layer 2 that settles to HyperEVM; it launched with a single Conduit-run sequencer, and its HyperCore market-data and order-routing hooks are planned for about four weeks after mainnet. Late on Nov 9 CST, Upbit, South Korea's largest exchange, announced HYPE trading against KRW, BTC and USDT from Nov 10 at 3 PM KST (midnight CST), with deposits and withdrawals only via HyperEVM and limit-only orders for the first two hours. Bithumb's same-day KRW listing is so far reported by outlets rather than confirmed from its own notice. Early Elysium activity figures circulating on X are unverified and not used here.
news.why: Hyperliquid gained a new execution layer that spends HYPE as gas and its first direct Korean-won route on the country's main exchange in the same day. Both widen access, but Elysium is still centrally sequenced without its HyperCore hooks, and a listing adds sellers as well as buyers.
news.tagReason: A confirmed L2 launch plus a top Korean exchange listing expand HYPE's use and access.
news.summary: Elysium mainnet launched Nov 9 with Bankr support, and Upbit opened HYPE KRW/BTC/USDT markets from Nov 10.

news.title: Acala and Karura propose shutting down on Feb 10, 2027
news.body: Acala announced on Nov 9 that it plans to wind down the Acala parachain on Polkadot and Karura on Kusama, and opened signalling referendums (Acala #195, Karura #137) to approve the plan. If they pass, withdrawals and XCM transfers stay open until Feb 10, 2027, when the chains stop producing blocks; LDOT must be unbonded by Jan 12 (Dec 16 for LDOT locked to specific validators) and LKSM by Feb 2. The team says it will try, as a last resort, to return leftover external assets to owners' Asset Hub accounts and donate treasury external assets to the Polkadot and Kusama treasuries. ACA and KAR cannot be withdrawn and stay on their chains. The team cites liquidity that never built up, fragmentation across parachains and usage that no longer covers running a dedicated chain.
news.why: Acala held Polkadot's first parachain slot and was its flagship DeFi hub, so its exit is a clear signal about parachain-era economics and DeFi fragmentation on Polkadot. DOT, USDT and USDC holders on Acala have firm deadlines, while the ecosystem's shift toward Asset Hub as the main liquidity venue continues.
news.tagReason: A founding Polkadot DeFi parachain is planning to shut down for lack of liquidity and usage.
news.summary: Acala and Karura propose a Feb 10, 2027 shutdown; LDOT unbonding deadlines start Dec 16.

news.title: NEAR AI pauses and restores its cloud after an SGLang-based intrusion
news.body: NEAR AI said on Nov 9 that it found unauthorized access to its internal systems and paused NEAR AI Cloud inference while it investigated. Its incident report says an attacker used a remote-code-execution flaw in SGLang, the open-source inference engine it runs, on Nov 8; about 100 users' account details were downloaded, 18 legacy agents' chat histories, settings and logs were accessed, and two Cloud API keys were exposed and revoked. NEAR AI patched every server, rotated credentials and brought the cloud back online late on Nov 9 CST. It says NEAR Protocol and other NEAR services were not affected.
news.why: NEAR is positioning private, user-owned AI as a core use case, so a breach of its AI cloud tests that pitch even though the chain itself was untouched. The fast disclosure and restoration limit the damage; the follow-up to watch is whether the report shows the enclave design kept customer prompts private.
news.tagReason: A confirmed security incident at NEAR's flagship AI service, though the protocol was unaffected.
news.summary: NEAR AI disclosed a Nov 8 intrusion via an SGLang flaw, paused NEAR AI Cloud and restored it; the protocol was unaffected.

news.title: Render's RNP-024 vote closes and Salad starts daily RENDER burns
news.body: The final vote on RNP-024, which funds Forth, a privacy-first AI gateway with incentives tied to paid usage, RENDER payments and Render compute, closed on Nov 9 at 5 PM PT (7 PM CST). The NATION tally shows about 143,300 RENDER for and none against; the proposal also requires participation of at least 15% of eligible supply, and Render had not posted an official result by early Nov 10, so the outcome is still unconfirmed here. Separately, Render said on Nov 9 that Salad has begun automated daily RENDER burns on Solana as testing ahead of RNP-023 Milestone 3. Render describes those burns as an early step toward full Burn-Mint Equilibrium settlement, which is still in development.
news.why: Forth would be Render's main new demand channel for AI work, and Salad's burns are the first live step in plugging an outside compute provider into Render's token economics. Both are early: Forth needs an official result and then paid usage, and the burns are tests rather than full settlement.
news.tagReason: Real governance and token-economics progress, but the vote result is unconfirmed and burns are in testing.
news.summary: RNP-024's final vote closed with only yes votes shown but no official result yet; Salad began test RENDER burns.

news.title: Binance withdrawal recovery keeps advancing route by route; NEAR is still a target
news.body: Binance kept reopening withdrawals one token-network pair at a time after its Oct 29 hot-wallet breach. Its Nov 8 morning update newly re-enabled HYPE and APT and listed Ethereum routes for QNT and ONDO and a Solana route for RENDER as already open, and a late Nov 8 update (10:56 PM CST) re-enabled Binance Alpha networks on BSC, Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum. No further reopening update was found on Nov 9. Binance's stated target for restoring NEAR and remaining assets is the end of this week, subject to security checks.
news.why: Exchange access is practical infrastructure for holders, applications and liquidity providers across this watchlist after the Oct 29 hot-wallet breach. Separating already-restored routes from genuinely new ones avoids overstating recovery, and NEAR remains an open follow-up rather than a completed milestone.
news.tagReason: Recovery is progressing, but remaining routes and the NEAR timetable are conditional.
news.summary: Binance keeps restoring withdrawals route by route (HYPE newly back Nov 8); NEAR remains a conditional target.

news.title: Fidelity Digital Assets report puts Solana at about 15% of major US exchange trades by count
news.body: Solana's official account on Nov 8 highlighted a Nov 6 Fidelity Digital Assets report, “Solana's Competitive Advantage in Onchain Trading,” by senior analyst Max Wadington. The report says Solana's decentralized exchanges handled about 15% of the trades Fidelity counted across major US exchanges in 2026, up from 0.30% in 2022, and briefly passed the NYSE in weekly executions. It also cites monthly tokenized-asset trading rising from under $100 million to nearly $5 billion and more than $590 billion of Solana perpetual-futures notional over 12 months. Fidelity is explicit that this is a trade-count comparison, not dollar value, and that the venues trade different instruments.
news.why: A major asset manager's research arm describing Solana as “an emerging piece of financial market infrastructure” is meaningful institutional validation of its trading and tokenization use case. The headline figure measures execution count, which flatters a high-throughput chain, so it is evidence of capacity and activity rather than share of US market value.
news.tagReason: Independent institutional research documents growing onchain trading and tokenized-asset activity, with a clear count-not-value caveat.
news.summary: Fidelity Digital Assets research, amplified by Solana on Nov 8, documents Solana's trade-count share and tokenized-asset growth.

news.title: Polkadot Referendum 1966 passes; the 500-validator change still awaits enactment
news.body: Referendum 1966, step one of Polkadot's validator set reduction, was confirmed on-chain late Nov 7. It sets the active validator count to 500, lowers the DAP validator incentive budget proportionally and adjusts related relay-chain and Coretime parameters. Subsquare showed about 2 days 4 hours left in the enactment period as of early Nov 9, which points to enactment around Nov 11 at relay block 33,814,400; that clock time is an estimate from block height. The smaller set applies from the first era after enactment, and later steps toward 400 and 320 need separate approval.
news.why: The change directly affects validator participation and the allocation of security resources, so enactment and the subsequent election deserve separate checks. A smaller validator set may change operational economics and concentration, but the vote itself does not prove either improved efficiency or impaired resilience.
news.tagReason: Approval is verified; actual enactment and downstream elections remain separate milestones.
news.summary: Polkadot approved the first validator reduction, but 500 active seats follow block-triggered enactment and the next applicable era.

news.title: Axelar Proposal 511 passes for Robinhood ITS trust configuration across 20 chains
news.body: Axelar’s governance explorer now marks Proposal 511 passed and voting closed, superseding the board’s prior pending-vote text. The proposal contains 20 contract-execution messages for Interchain Token Service trusted-chain configuration involving the chain identifier robinhood. Named destinations include Ethereum, Base, Hedera and xrpl-evm, among others. The governance result does not independently verify successful destination-chain execution, operational token transfers or a new consumer-facing Robinhood product.
news.why: Trust configuration is a concrete prerequisite for cross-chain token routing and is more specific than a generic interoperability announcement. For AXL, the next evidence should be successful execution and actual application traffic; the Hedera and XRPL EVM references should not be confused with a new native-XRPL feature.
news.tagReason: A completed governance approval advances integration configuration, with execution still unverified.
news.summary: Axelar approved 20 ITS trust-configuration calls, not independently verified live transfers on every destination.

news.title: NEAR’s hackathon enters its final submission week with Intents and agent-building tracks
news.body: NEAR’s November 7 reminder gives builders until November 14 at 5:59 PM CST to submit working projects. The official site lists $250,000 in prizes across 13 tracks, including cross-chain DeFi, autonomous businesses, privacy and AI security. Submissions require a public repository and a public demo post, with judging and results scheduled for November 16–18. The event is an active builder program, not proof that the resulting prototypes will become maintained applications or generate recurring settlement.
news.why: The tracks create a near-term test of whether NEAR Intents, Chain Signatures and AI-related tooling can be turned into usable products. The strongest follow-through will be working demonstrations, maintained code and retained users after prizes are awarded, rather than submission counts alone.
news.tagReason: A verified active builder program has a concrete deadline; adoption outcomes are still ahead.
news.summary: NEAR’s builder program closes November 14 at 5:59 PM CST, with post-event product retention still to be tested.

news.title: AWS launches Nitro Sandboxes for hardware-isolated pods, tasks and AI agents
news.body: AWS said on Nov 9 that Nitro Sandboxes are now available as lightweight virtual machines managed by the Nitro Hypervisor, so each Amazon EKS pod, ECS task or lightweight VM, including AI agents, can run in its own hardware-isolated environment. AWS says workloads run at near-native EC2 performance and can be validated through cryptographic attestation, so secrets are released only to sandboxes that prove their integrity. Turning it on in EKS or ECS is described as a one-line change, and Amazon Linux and Firecracker are natively supported. It is available on most Nitro-based EC2 instances in all commercial regions at no additional charge.
news.why: Safely running untrusted, LLM-generated code is a core requirement for agentic AI, and AWS is building that isolation into its standard compute at no extra cost. It strengthens AWS's pitch for hosting AI agents and multi-tenant workloads, which matters for the AI and compute backdrop that decentralized compute networks compete against.
news.tagReason: A generally available, no-cost security feature aimed squarely at AI-agent workloads.
news.summary: AWS made Nitro Sandboxes generally available on Nov 9 for hardware-isolated EKS pods, ECS tasks and AI agents at no extra charge.

news.title: NVIDIA introduces GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at the Conference on Robot Learning
news.body: NVIDIA said on Nov 9 at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin that it is introducing GR00T 2, an open world action model for robots built on NVIDIA Cosmos and trained partly on 100,000 hours of open human egocentric data. NVIDIA reports it reached 71% average success across 50 tasks with one demonstration per task, rising to 95% with five; those are NVIDIA's own figures. It also released Isaac Lab 3.0, which it says delivers up to 2.5 times the training throughput of the prior version on one benchmark, plus new open benchmarks DexBench and VABAR. Foxconn, Siemens and Nexuni are named as testing or evaluating GR00T 2.
news.why: Robotics is one of NVIDIA's next demand stories beyond data-center training, and open models plus simulation tools pull developers onto its GPUs and software stack. Results are company-reported and early, so the signal is ecosystem momentum rather than revenue.
news.tagReason: A meaningful open-model and tooling release, with performance claims that are self-reported.
news.summary: NVIDIA unveiled the open GR00T 2 robot model, Isaac Lab 3.0 and new benchmarks at CoRL on Nov 9.

news.title: AMD EPYC CPUs host Google Cloud's TPU 8tx, the first cloud TPU with confidential computing
news.body: AMD said on Nov 9 that 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors power the host infrastructure for Google Cloud TPU 8tx, which both companies describe as the first cloud TPU system with hardware-enforced confidential computing. The EPYC chips handle orchestration, data preparation and communication with the TPUs, and AMD's Secure Encrypted Virtualization extends protection to the connected accelerators so prompts, model weights and intermediate data stay encrypted in memory and in transit. Google Cloud's Mark Lohmeyer is quoted saying this brings confidential computing to cloud TPUs for the first time. AMD also says EPYC is the host CPU for more than 10 leading hyperscalers and frontier AI labs.
news.why: It ties AMD's server CPUs into Google's in-house AI chip platform, not just GPU systems, and gives Google a security feature aimed at enterprises moving sensitive AI agents into production. Confidential AI compute is the same problem decentralized AI networks pitch to solve, so it is useful context for the AI and compute coins.
news.tagReason: A jointly confirmed product launch that expands both companies' AI infrastructure roles.
news.summary: AMD EPYC now hosts Google Cloud TPU 8tx, the first cloud TPU system with hardware-enforced confidential computing.

news.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a low-cost model for high-volume agent work
news.body: Meta introduced Muse Ember on Nov 9, its smallest and most efficient model, built for repeated agent tasks such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing. It is available on the Meta Model API and Muse Code at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window. Meta says it is the first model trained using Muse Wonder Full and cites Artificial Analysis results placing it on the cost-efficiency frontier; several comparisons are Meta's own evaluations. Box, Cline, Oracle, Cloudflare and You.com are quoted from early testing, and Meta says its Muse models are now available on Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud.
news.why: Meta is competing on price for the agent workloads that drive most AI token volume, and selling through other clouds widens its reach beyond its own apps. Cheaper agent models lower costs across the AI stack, which matters for the backdrop around decentralized AI and compute networks.
news.tagReason: A generally available paid model with named enterprise testers, though some benchmarks are self-reported.
news.summary: Meta launched Muse Ember on Nov 9, a low-cost agent model priced at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens.

news.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after reports Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort
news.body: Nvidia's board said on Nov 8 that independent directors, working with outside counsel, will oversee an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. In a company-wide email published by CNBC, Huang apologized to his family and employees for a personal relationship, said he would cooperate fully and reaffirmed his commitment to Nvidia and US national security. The board said it continues to support Huang's leadership while the review proceeds. Republican lawmakers had earlier asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on the matter, and the review's scope and timing have not been published.
news.why: This is a governance and policy-risk story for the most important AI-chip supplier, arriving days before Nvidia's Nov 17 results and amid tighter scrutiny of chip exports to China. Nvidia has no verified direct crypto exposure, so it matters here for the AI and compute backdrop rather than any watchlist network.
news.tagReason: A board-level investigation adds governance and regulatory uncertainty; no wrongdoing has been established.
news.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Nov 8; Huang apologized to staff and said he will cooperate.

researchSummary.body: The Nov 7–9 window leans constructive, led by institutional distribution. Solana gained a filed SEC-exemption venue for tokenized US equities and a Schwab Crypto listing on the same day, NEAR Intents went live inside Talos's institutional trading system, and Hyperliquid got its Elysium Layer 2 plus a Upbit won listing. Governance moved toward execution at Polkadot and Axelar, but Polkadot also lost its flagship DeFi parachain to a proposed Acala shutdown, and Render's RNP-024 result is still unconfirmed. Security cautions sit in adjacent services rather than core protocols: the NEAR AI cloud intrusion, Binance's still-incomplete withdrawal recovery, and market-wide incidents at Ankr, LNbits, Keplr/Web3Auth and Initia. None of this establishes a price outcome, and it is not financial advice.

weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 2–8, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week’s strongest ecosystem theme was wider distribution with important boundaries around what is actually live. Coinbase corroborated Bankr’s exchange-account connection, Chutes listed Tencent Hy4 behind a live API, and Hedera’s McLaren collectibles gained an accessible secondary market. Sui reiterated a forthcoming Samsung Wallet USDC rollout, while Ondo’s Anthropic announcement remained a conditional IPO-day plan rather than a completed issuance. Stellar’s RWA milestone was supported by a dated issuer dashboard; those asset balances should not be confused with payments, active users or governance-token cash flows.

Governance and security required more precise stage labels. Polkadot Referendum 1966 moved into enactment, while Axelar Proposal 511 passed without independent confirmation of execution on every destination chain. ICP’s GuestOS election remains open, and Render’s Forth proposal is still in final voting. Bittensor’s post-quantum wallet code is deployed but the reviewed documentation still gates spending, whereas Firelight’s November 5 Lido integration is live under defined cover periods, exclusions and capital limits. Algorand’s grants and community reset is the main negative operational change: staking commitments remain, but builder-support structures contract.

Market infrastructure remains the cross-watchlist caution. Binance continues staged restoration and still supplies only a conditional NEAR target, while Treasury’s MEXC order introduces a future restriction on US financial-institution transfers. The Keplr / Web3Auth narrative also changed materially: recovery-wallet attribution means the observed $6.01 million cannot be reported as a verified theft. This recap is a source-verified slice of the week, not exhaustive coverage, and separates releases, approvals, execution and measured usage. It contains no trading recommendation or price forecast.

stocks.name: Tesla, Inc.
stocks.overview: Tesla builds electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and is investing heavily in self-driving (FSD, Robotaxi and the Cybercab), Optimus robots and its own AI compute. In Q3 2026 revenue was $28.05 billion, roughly flat year over year, with 486,532 deliveries (down about 2%) and net income attributable to common stockholders of $787 million ($0.22 per diluted share), down from $1.37 billion a year earlier; energy revenue fell 16% while services and other rose 33%. Recent moves include Cybercab service starting in Austin in September, a new €100 million Berlin engineering center that opened Nov 4 with about 250 staff, and an official Argentina launch set for Nov 20. Shareholders meet on Dec 3, and Tesla and SpaceX have discussed a possible combination, though no terms have been announced and any deal would need shareholder approval. The main near-term risk is political: after Democrats won Congress and Texas, Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Nov 5, as investors priced in possible congressional probes and tighter rules on AI data centers.
stocks.researchSummary: Tesla's latest quarter showed flat revenue and lower profit, with a pivot in spending toward AI compute, robotaxis and robots. This week's company news was constructive (the Berlin engineering hub and the Argentina entry), but after the midterms the bigger story is the regulatory and political overhang on Elon Musk's companies.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
stocks.overview: AMD makes EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI GPUs, Ryzen PC chips and embedded and gaming silicon. Q3 2026 revenue was a record $13.4 billion (+45%), data center revenue nearly doubled (+97%) to $8.5 billion on the MI450 launch and EPYC demand, and diluted EPS was $1.46 GAAP and $2.09 non-GAAP. Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773 million. AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion ±3% as it scales Helios rack systems and 'Venice' CPUs, and it filed its 10-Q on Nov 4. It is scheduled to present at the UBS conference on Dec 1 and Barclays on Dec 9. The main risk is AI-spending sentiment and supply: AMD shares fell double digits on Nov 5 in the post-midterm chip selloff, and the memory shortage is raising component costs.
stocks.researchSummary: AMD's latest quarter was its strongest on record and it is now mainly a data-center company, with guidance for faster growth in Q4. The stock's sharp drop on Nov 5 reflected sector-wide fears about the AI build-out rather than company-specific news.

flags.text: CNBC links the post-election chip selloff to concerns over data-center restrictions and power-cost rules: voters opposed data centers in all but one of 41 local ballot measures.

AMD competes with Nvidia in AI accelerators and with Intel in CPUs. CNBC notes that the global memory shortage is pushing up costs for AMD, Intel and Qualcomm, and AMD's gaming revenue fell 40% in Q3.
Data Center was $8.5 billion of $13.4 billion in Q3 revenue (about 64%), so AMD is increasingly tied to AI and cloud capex cycles.

stocks.name: Intel Corporation
stocks.overview: Intel designs and manufactures PC and server CPUs and is building a contract foundry business (Intel 14A). Q3 2026 revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion (its strongest growth in 15 years) and Intel Foundry revenue rose 58%, with GAAP EPS of $0.60 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52. Q4 guidance is $15.0–16.0 billion of revenue, with an expected PC slowdown through at least the first half of 2027. Recent deals include a multiyear Xeon collaboration with Oracle Cloud, a planned acquisition of Classiq (quantum software) and a $23 billion equity offering. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (Form 4 filed Nov 4). The main risks are supply and execution: an accident at the Kiryat Gat fab in Israel will cost about $300 million of Q4 revenue, with a similar hit expected in Q1.
stocks.researchSummary: Intel's data-center demand is outrunning its supply, but a weaker PC outlook and the Israel fab accident produced soft guidance. The CEO's open-market purchase is a notable insider signal, though it is not a forecast.

flags.text: Intel lists the U.S. government's acquisition of significant equity interests in the company, along with export controls and trade policy, among its key risk factors.

Intel says demand for its data-center products 'continues to meaningfully exceed available supply', limited by Intel 3 yields, substrate shortages and the Fab 28 accident, which will cut about $300 million from Q4 revenue and 200 basis points from gross margin.

The turnaround rests on CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has bought shares personally (150,000 on Nov 2). Client computing is still about half of Intel Products revenue ($8.1 billion of $15.4 billion), which leaves Intel exposed to the PC slowdown.

stocks.name: Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS)
stocks.overview: Amazon is the parent of AWS, the largest cloud provider, alongside its retail, Prime, advertising, devices and newer businesses (Zoox, Amazon Leo satellites, Pharmacy). In Q3 2026 AWS revenue rose 39% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years and a $184 billion annualized run rate, with $17.8 billion of operating income (38.7% margin). Total net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, operating income was a record $28.1 billion and EPS was $1.89. AWS signed new agreements with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Oracle and others, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17x and Trainium became easier to adopt through TorchNeuron; CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. On Nov 5 Amazon launched $0 Uber Eats delivery for Prime members, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30–Dec 4 in Las Vegas. The main risk is capital intensity: 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion.
stocks.researchSummary: AWS is accelerating on AI demand and is the main driver of Amazon's profits, while retail margins hit a record. The trade-off is very heavy AI capex funded partly with new debt, plus rising data-center permitting risk in the U.S.
stocks.cryptoLink: AWS stopped accepting new customers for Amazon Managed Blockchain (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Polygon node access) on Oct 29, 2026, and will end the service on Sep 29, 2027, pointing users to self-managed Node Runners on AWS or partners such as Alchemy and QuickNode.

flags.text: Voters sided against data centers in all but one of 41 local ballot measures on Nov 3, and CNBC reports that the hyperscalers, Amazon included, fell 2–4% on Nov 5 on build-out concerns.

Trailing-12-month free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4 billion and long-term debt rose to $173.1 billion from $65.6 billion at end-2025, as AWS competes with Google Cloud, whose revenue grew 103%, and Microsoft for AI capacity.
AWS generated $17.8 billion of Amazon's $28.1 billion Q3 operating income (about 63%), so group profit depends heavily on cloud and AI demand.
